This notebook goes with Lectures 11a (matching, `Fall/L9 - Quasi Experiments/L9d - Matching.pdf`) and 11b
(synthetic control, `L10a - Synthetic Control.pdf`). It leaves you five short problems. The membership program is

Everything is simulated, so you always know the right answer.

# Part 1: Selection on observables (Lecture 11a)

## Reproduce: a paid membership program

An online retailer sells a paid membership (free shipping, member prices). Customers choose whether to join, and
the ones who join are heavier past spenders, have been customers longer, and use the app. The outcome is spending
next quarter, in dollars. The effect of membership is larger for heavier spenders, so the ATT and the ATE differ.

Conditional independence holds *by construction*: membership depends only on the three observed covariates. `sel`
scales how strongly past spending drives membership.

```{r}
sim_members <- function(N = 4000, sel = 1.2) {
  past <- rnorm(N, 0, 1)                         # standardized log past spend
  tenure <- rexp(N, 1 / 3)                       # years as a customer
  app <- rbinom(N, 1, 0.4)                       # uses the mobile app
  ps <- plogis(-1 + sel * past + 0.15 * tenure + 0.8 * app)
  D <- rbinom(N, 1, ps)
  tau_i <- 30 + 20 * past                        # heterogeneous effect, $ per quarter
  y0 <- 200 + 60 * past + 15 * past^2 + 5 * tenure + 20 * app + rnorm(N, 0, 40)
  data.frame(past, tenure, app, D, ps_true = ps, tau_i, y = y0 + tau_i * D)
}
m <- sim_members()
truth <- c(ATE = mean(m$tau_i), ATT = mean(m$tau_i[m$D == 1]))
truth
```

Balance before adjustment, in standardized differences (the slides' $d_k$):

```{r}
std_diff <- function(x, D, w = rep(1, length(x))) {
  m1 <- weighted.mean(x[D == 1], w[D == 1]); m0 <- weighted.mean(x[D == 0], w[D == 0])
  (m1 - m0) / sqrt((var(x[D == 1]) + var(x[D == 0])) / 2)
}
covs <- c("past", "tenure", "app")
round(sapply(covs, function(v) std_diff(m[[v]], m$D)), 2)
```

Estimators of the ATT and ATE. The propensity score is a logit on the three covariates. Matching is one nearest
neighbor on the estimated score, with replacement. The regression-adjustment and AIPW outcome models fit each arm
separately with a quadratic in past spending.

```{r}
m$ps <- fitted(glm(D ~ past + tenure + app, binomial, m))
treated <- which(m$D == 1); controls <- which(m$D == 0)

# 1-NN matching on the propensity score (ATT)
oc <- controls[order(m$ps[controls])]; pos <- findInterval(m$ps[treated], m$ps[oc])
lo <- oc[pmax(pos, 1)]; hi <- oc[pmin(pos + 1, length(oc))]
nn <- ifelse(abs(m$ps[lo] - m$ps[treated]) <= abs(m$ps[hi] - m$ps[treated]), lo, hi)
att_nn <- mean(m$y[treated] - m$y[nn])

# IPW (Hajek). ATT: controls weighted by ps / (1 - ps). ATE: both arms reweighted.
w_att <- ifelse(m$D == 1, 1, m$ps / (1 - m$ps))
att_ipw <- weighted.mean(m$y[treated], w_att[treated]) - weighted.mean(m$y[controls], w_att[controls])
w_ate <- ifelse(m$D == 1, 1 / m$ps, 1 / (1 - m$ps))
ate_ipw <- weighted.mean(m$y[treated], w_ate[treated]) - weighted.mean(m$y[controls], w_ate[controls])

# Outcome models by arm, then AIPW (ATE)
mu <- function(arm, f = y ~ past + I(past^2) + tenure + app) predict(lm(f, m[m$D == arm, ]), m)
mu1 <- mu(1); mu0 <- mu(0)
ate_ra <- mean(mu1 - mu0)
att_ra <- mean(m$y[treated] - mu0[treated])
aipw <- function(mu1, mu0, ps) mean(mu1 - mu0 + m$D * (m$y - mu1) / ps - (1 - m$D) * (m$y - mu0) / (1 - ps))
ate_aipw <- aipw(mu1, mu0, m$ps)

data.frame(
  estimator = c("Difference in means", "OLS: y on D + covariates (linear)", "1-NN on propensity score",
                "IPW (Hajek)", "Regression adjustment by arm", "IPW (Hajek)", "Regression adjustment by arm", "AIPW"),
  estimand = c("-", "-", "ATT", "ATT", "ATT", "ATE", "ATE", "ATE"),
  estimate = round(c(mean(m$y[treated]) - mean(m$y[controls]), coef(feols(y ~ D + past + tenure + app, m))["D"],
                     att_nn, att_ipw, att_ra, ate_ipw, ate_ra, ate_aipw), 1),
  truth = round(c(NA, NA, rep(truth["ATT"], 3), rep(truth["ATE"], 3)), 1))
```

Each estimate carries sampling noise. Over 200 simulated samples, all six adjusted estimators are centered on their
truth; their standard deviations run from about \$1.5 (regression adjustment, AIPW) to \$3 (matching), \$4 (IPW for
the ATE) and \$7 (IPW for the ATT). Matching and weighting buy robustness to the outcome model at a price in variance.

Balance after weighting for the ATT:

```{r}
round(sapply(covs, function(v) std_diff(m[[v]], m$D, w_att)), 3)
```

# Part 2: Synthetic control (Lecture 11b)

## Reproduce: a city soda tax

The design in the slides: one treated city, 40 donor cities, 24 quarters, and a tax that cuts per-capita sales by
10% from quarter 17. Sales follow a two-factor model; the treated city loads $0.75$ on the trend factor, inside
the donors' range. `alpha1` shifts the treated city's *level*.

```{r}
sim_soda <- function(J = 40, Tq = 24, T0 = 16, mu1 = 0.75, alpha1 = 0, sd_alpha = 0) {
  lam <- cbind(seq(0, 2, length.out = Tq), rnorm(Tq))
  mu <- matrix(runif((J + 1) * 2), J + 1, 2); mu[1, ] <- c(mu1, 0.3)
  alpha <- c(alpha1, rnorm(J, 0, sd_alpha))
  Y <- 100 + matrix(alpha, Tq, J + 1, byrow = TRUE) + 5 * lam %*% t(mu) + matrix(rnorm(Tq * (J + 1)), Tq, J + 1)
  truth <- -0.1 * mean(Y[(T0 + 1):Tq, 1]); Y[(T0 + 1):Tq, 1] <- 0.9 * Y[(T0 + 1):Tq, 1]
  list(Y = Y, T0 = T0, truth = truth)           # Y is quarters x cities; city 1 is treated
}
sc_w <- function(y1, Y0) solve.QP(crossprod(Y0) + diag(1e-8, ncol(Y0)), crossprod(Y0, y1),
                                  cbind(1, diag(ncol(Y0))), c(1, rep(0, ncol(Y0))), meq = 1)$solution
s <- sim_soda(); Y <- s$Y; T0 <- s$T0; post <- (T0 + 1):nrow(Y)
w <- sc_w(Y[1:T0, 1], Y[1:T0, -1])
gap <- Y[, 1] - Y[, -1] %*% w
round(w[w > 0.05], 2)
c(sc = mean(gap[post]), truth = s$truth, pre_rmspe = sqrt(mean(gap[1:T0]^2)))

matplot(Y, type = "l", lty = 1, col = "grey85", xlab = "quarter", ylab = "sales per capita")
lines(Y[, 1], lwd = 2, col = "#1f4e79"); lines(Y[, -1] %*% w, lwd = 2, lty = 2, col = "#bb0000")
abline(v = T0 + 0.5, lty = 3)
legend("topleft", bty = "n", legend = c("treated city", "synthetic city", "donors"),
       col = c("#1f4e79", "#bb0000", "grey70"), lwd = c(2, 2, 1), lty = c(1, 2, 1))
```

DiD, SC and synthetic DiD side by side with `synthdid` (which wants units in rows, controls first):

```{r}
three <- function(Y, T0) {
  Ys <- t(Y)[c(2:ncol(Y), 1), ]; N0 <- ncol(Y) - 1
  c(did = did_estimate(Ys, N0, T0), sc = sc_estimate(Ys, N0, T0), sdid = synthdid_estimate(Ys, N0, T0))
}
round(c(three(Y, T0), truth = s$truth), 2)
```
